findings.title: Trade row mapping is positional, unlike the candle mapping
findings.description: `CandleRecord.from_row` walks `CANDLE_COLUMNS`, so a column change in the repository is followed automatically. `TradeRecord.from_row` instead reads `values[0]` through `values[7]` by index. The indexes depend on the order of `TRADE_COLUMNS` minus `market_ticker`, as computed in `serve_timeseries.TRADE_VALUE_COLUMNS`. If a column is added or reordered, the fields shift silently, and Pydantic validation may not catch a swap between same-typed fields such as `yes_price_dollars` and `no_price_dollars`. The integration test only checks the value count, not which field gets which value. Build the record from `zip(TRADE_VALUE_COLUMNS, row.values)` as keyword arguments. Otherwise add a test that asserts the name-to-slot mapping.

findings.title: `_window` infers the period predicate from whether `extra` is truthy
findings.description: The helper adds `period = %(period)s` whenever `extra` is non-empty. It does not check that `extra` actually contains `period`. A future caller passing any other extra parameter would get a `period` clause with no bound value, which fails at runtime. The coupling is implicit. Make the period an explicit argument, or pass extra predicates as `sql.Composable` along with their params.

findings.title: `tape_filtered` depends on a parameter name inside `trades_filter_sql`
findings.description: The function reads `selection.params["trades_excluded_categories"]` and re-implements the `COALESCE(category, '')` semantics in Python. This reuses the parameter set but not the logic, so the claim that the two cannot drift is only partly true. A rename of the key raises `KeyError` at request time. A shape-guard `TypeError` is marked `pragma: no cover`. The parametrized integration test comparing the helper with the SQL predicate does reduce the risk. Consider having `selection` export the excluded-category set or a pure predicate function, so both consumers share it.

findings.title: Load test reaches into private pool state and uses a class-level mutable list
findings.description: The recording-cursor setup touches `pool._pool` (suppressed with `# noqa: SLF001`) and sets `cursor_factory` on live connections. `_RecordingCursor.statements` is shared class state. This is fragile across psycopg_pool upgrades, and connections created after setup, such as pool growth, would not be recorded. In assertion 2 that could produce a false pass on "no fetch". The current pool size and test shape make it unlikely to matter today. Prefer a pool `configure` callback, or pass the cursor factory through the app's pool construction.

findings.title: Length and structure
findings.description: The load test file is about 360 lines and `test/load/conftest.py` grew by about 150 lines, both over the ~300-line guideline. The seeding function `_seed_kalshi_dense` is also long. Splitting the Kalshi seeding into `kalshi_support` would match how the schema helpers were already moved there.

findings.title: Window resolution, ceiling guard and connection scoping
findings.description: The refusal is raised after the executor call returns, so the pooled connection is released before the 422. Window helpers were extracted into `windows.py` rather than duplicated between the bars and Kalshi routes. The count-before-fetch design is tested at the unit level (no fetch call on refusal) and at the load level. Unit tests cover the 404, 422, empty-window facts, naive datetimes, bare dates and msgpack paths. The `try/except` rules are not violated anywhere in the diff.
